phpunit.xml forces APP_ENV=testing (line 27) and isProduction() is a strict container-'env' check, so after this change the OTP flow is UNREACHABLE in the test suite by default. The worker added a withProductionEnvironment() helper and wrapped the 4 pre-existing tests whose assertions only hold when the OTP step actually runs (test_sends_otp, test_client_org_user_with_active_access_grant_can_request_otp_without_client_role, test_repo_org_user_with_hotlist_enabled_authenticates_to_app, test_authenticate_with_invalid_otp). Diff reviewed by the driver: every assertion is preserved verbatim, only re-indented into the closure — no assertion weakened or dropped.
isProduction() honors the container 'env' binding, NOT config('app.env') — the helper sets app()['env'] and restores it in a finally. Worth knowing for any future environment-gated test.

All three RN3 lanes reported phpunit hanging 8-25 min and filed it as environment trouble; one ran a control test untouched by the diff and confirmed it hung too. Root cause found by the driver: the lanes each ran --filter CustomLoginPageTest concurrently against the SAME zod_testing_claude_dev_2521 database and deadlocked on platform.permissions_id_seq / permissions (Lock:transactionid + Lock:relation), and the orphaned processes kept the locks after the lanes ended. Killed 7 orphan PIDs; the suite then ran in 5.7s. Not a code defect. The RN4 lane was explicitly told not to run the suite.

Teardown env_restore hazard. Reverting the recorded .env keys put CLICKHOUSE_HOST back to the production ClickHouse Cloud cluster together with a real CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD, because that was their pre-QA value (bootstrap copies them in). The worktree survives teardown, so this would have left live production CH credentials wired into it - the exact thing the never-wire-Cloud-into-a-worktree rule forbids. Driver re-neutralized CLICKHOUSE_HOST to 127.0.0.1 and cleared both CH passwords after the restore. env_restore should not carry CLICKHOUSE_HOST or CH credentials.

findings_residual.summary: The PR-preview workflow's `staging` target overrides QA_DB_HOST to the PRODUCTION DB host while hardcoding APP_ENV: preprod. With this change merged, a staging-target preview is a VPC-reachable app on production data where any known panel-eligible email logs in with no password and no OTP. This falsifies the premise of the operator's approved Q3 answer ('preprod holds non-production data behind the VPC'). Remediation is outside the two touched files: either set a production-valued APP_ENV on the staging target, or remove the staging/prod-DB option. MATERIAL - requires an operator decision, not auto-answerable.

loginViaOtp() calls assertNotProduction(baseURL) and then hard-waits 15s for an OTP field the bypass now prevents from rendering, so the helper throws in every environment it is permitted to run in. Breaks 6 committed spec files (unique-scans-to-case-claims, missed-opportunities, staging-live-hit-leader, lpr-repossessions, unique-lpr-case-claims, unique-scans-leaderboard). Also contradicts the helper's own docblock ('Always uses the real OTP form'). No Playwright CI job exists, so CI stays green and this surfaces only on the next manual `npm run test:e2e`. Fix is small: branch on OTP-field visibility / early-return once the URL leaves /login, and update the docblock.

findings_adjudicated_not_fixed.detail: Claim: the production-data fix covers only the Postgres axis; ClickHouse is excluded by assertion. Driver read the GitHub Actions variables: QA_CLICKHOUSE_HOST = zd69ju2h8d.us-east-2.aws.clickhouse.cloud, i.e. the production ClickHouse Cloud cluster with the literal clarity/zod databases. The FACT is correct. But kamal-deploy.yml:94 uses the same variable, so pre-platform and every preview have ALWAYS read production ClickHouse, and CLICKHOUSE_WRITE_USERNAME falls back to the read-only CLICKHOUSE_USERNAME. Pre-existing and deliberate, not introduced by this diff; making preprod login frictionless IS this ticket and pre-platform is its target. Recorded as accepted risk. Follow-up noted: kamal-pr-preview.yml:319 prints 'ClickHouse stays QA in every target', which is misleading about a security-relevant fact.

Driver read it: the staging GitHub environment defines MAIL_MAILER=smtp, MAIL_HOST=sandbox.smtp.mailtrap.io, MAIL_PORT=2525, MAIL_USERNAME. Mail works; the target retains a login path.
